facts.statement: Guanlingsaurus reached a maximum length of 8.3 meters and possessed a wide, triangular skull with a short, toothless snout.
facts.quote: It grew up to 8.3 m in length and has a wide, triangular skull with a short and toothless snout.

facts.statement: This extinct shastasaurid ichthyosaur lived in China during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: Guanlingsaurus is an extinct genus of shastasaurid ichthyosaur from the Late Triassic of China.

facts.statement: Guanlingsaurus was first named in 2000 based on an incomplete adult skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus and species were first named in 2000 on the basis of an incomplete adult skeleton.

facts.statement: More complete skeletons were described in 2011, and a complete juvenile skeleton was described in 2013.
facts.quote: More complete skeletons were described in 2011, and a complete skeleton belonging to a juvenile was described in 2013.

facts.statement: Some sources state that Guanlingsaurus grew to approximately 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: Crecía hasta unos 10 metros de longitud

facts.statement: Fossil evidence dates Guanlingsaurus to the Carnian age, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Both adult and juvenile Guanlingsaurus specimens completely lacked teeth and did not possess a dental groove.
facts.quote: Both adult and juvenile specimens of Guanlingsaurus completely lack teeth and do not even possess a dental groove.

facts.statement: The very short snout of Guanlingsaurus was highly compressed through a unique arrangement of skull bones.
facts.quote: The very short snout was highly compressed via a unique arrangement of skull bones.

facts.statement: Typicusichthyosaurus tsaihuae was proposed as a synonym for Guanlingsaurus in 2000.
facts.quote: synonyms: Typicusichthyosaurus tsaihuae? Yin et al., 2000

facts.statement: Guanlingsaurus is classified within the family Shastasauridae.

rejected.statement: The species was temporarily reassigned to the genus Shastasaurus in 2011 but was reinstated in 2013 after a juvenile specimen revealed distinct features.
rejected.quote: In 2011 Guanlingsaurus liangae was reassigned to the genus Shastasaurus... However, the description of the juvenile specimen in 2013 revealed several features that make G. liangae distinct from Shastasaurus species, and the name was reinstated.

rejected.statement: Researchers disagree on the extent of the nasal bones and the suitability of Guanlingsaurus for suction feeding, with some suggesting the snout extended to the tip while others found the hyoid bone too short for such feeding.
rejected.quote: In 2011, Sander and colleagues interpreted the nasal bones... as extending to the very tip of the snout... However, Ji and colleagues did not find this feature, and found the hyoid bone much shorter than previous estimation, indicating that it was not suitable for suction feeding.
